claim: Cycling Through the Trees (Fietsen door de Bomen) in Pijnven/Bosland is only 12 km by bike from Lommel center, with suggested routes starting at Parking de Soeverein (node 224, 38.7 km loop) or Parking House of Nature (50.7 km loop).
quote: From the center of Lommel it is only 12 km by bike to the iconic bike bridge... Full route (50.7 km): Begins at Parking House of Nature (between nodes 224-230); Shorter alternative (38.7 km): Starts at Parking Soeverein (node 224)

claim: The double circular bridge in Pijnven rises gradually to 10 m so cyclists ride 700 m through the treetops at node 272, address Kiefhoekstraat 16, Hechtel-Eksel, with free parking; the installation opened June 2019 and travel is one-directional.
quote: Via a double circular bicycle bridge, you gradually rise to a height of 10 meters, where you cycle among the treetops, and the 700-meter route takes you through a wonderful world of green... Opened June 2019... Free parking available at the site

claim: The official Visit Limburg Cycling Through the Trees route is 38 km on flat terrain, starting at junction 272 in Hechtel-Eksel, passing the German military cemetery in Lommel, with downloadable GPX and PDF map.
quote: Route Length: 38 km; Difficulty: Flat terrain; Starting Point: Junction 272 in Hechtel-Eksel... Passes the German military cemetery in Lommel

claim: Cycling Through Water (Fietsen door het Water) is at node 91 in Bokrijk (Pad z/n, 3600 Genk), a 200+ m path through a pond with water at eye level, accessible to walkers/joggers with two car parks at Bokrijklaan 1.
quote: Cycling through Water in Bokrijk is a unique cycling experience in which you cycle more than 200 meters through a pond... node 91 of the cycle node network in Bokrijk... Enter Bokrijklaan 1, 3600 Genk as the GPS address

claim: A Lommel-to-Bokrijk cycling route covers 43.66 km, putting the Cycling Through Water installation well outside a 30 km radius from Cuchara (driving distance is similar at 44.4 km).
quote: A cycling route from Lommel to Bokrijk is 43.66 km... For reference, the driving distance between Bokrijk and Lommel is 44.4 km

claim: Cycling Through the Heathland is in Maasmechelen between nodes 550-551 in Hoge Kempen National Park, a 4 km route with a ~300 m wooden bridge over 700 ha of Mechelse Heide; no parking at the bridge itself — visitors park at Terhills, De Lieteberg, Station As, Kattevennen or Pietersheim gateways.
quote: Location/Town: Maasmechelen, within Hoge Kempen National Park... Route Length: 4 kilometers; Starting Node Points: Cycle nodes 550-551... No parking available at the trailhead itself. Visitors must park at designated gateway entrances: Terhills Maasmechelen...

claim: Limburg's fietsroutenetwerk covers 1,800+ km of signposted cycling routes connected by numbered knooppunten on blue eye-level signs; the node system was invented in Belgian Limburg by mine engineer Hugo Bollen after the 1980s coal-mine closures.
quote: The cycling route network of Fietsparadijs Limburg consists of more than 1,800 km of cycling routes, connected via knooppunten... When coal mines in Belgian Limburg closed in the 1980s, mine engineer Hugo Bollen proposed a project to create a cycling and walking route network

claim: A 16.5 km child-friendly Sahara loop runs from Parking Soeverein (Speelpleinstraat 77, Lommel) via nodes 224-230-231-232-260-224, paved with only 15 m elevation, visiting the House of Nature sculpture, Bocholt-Herentals canal, pedestrian bridge, Blauwe Kei and the Sahara dunes/blue lake.
quote: Route Length: 16.5 km... cycling nodes 224–230–231–232–260–224... Parking de Soeverein is available at Speelpleinstraat 77, 3920 Lommel... House of Nature sculpture (7.5m high, 50m wide)... easy difficulty level with only 15m elevation gain

claim: Nationaal Park Bosland offers the Mountainbikenetwerk Noord-Limburg with 270 km of signposted MTB trails across Lommel, Peer, Pelt, Hechtel-Eksel, Bocholt and Hamont-Achel, plus five combinable MTB loops in Lommel (Kattenbos, Sahara, Heuvelse Heide).
quote: Mountainbikenetwerk Noord-Limburg - A comprehensive network spanning 270 kilometers through the Sahara and Pijnven areas, connecting Lommel, Peer, Pelt, Hechtel-Eksel, Bocholt, and Hamont-Achel... MTB routes in Lommel - Five loops, some combinable

claim: BoslandBike 2026 (Sunday 26 April) is a gravel/MTB festival starting at Forestique (Witherendreef 1, 3900 Pelt), with 100 km gravel and MTB courses (€39.50) and 10/25/50 km family routes (€5); registration opened 1 November 2025.
quote: BoslandBike occurs on Sunday, April 26, 2026, in and around National Park Bosland. The event starts and finishes at Forestique (Witherendreef 1, 3900 Pelt)... Gravel 100km (€39.50)... Family Routes (€5.00) - Distances: 10km, 25km, or 50km

claim: Recommended Hechtel-Eksel rides include the Cycling Through the Trees - Butterfly Valley Lommel Loop (16.2 km, easy, starts at Natuurreservaat Veewei) and the 18.1 km De Boom In by Will Beckers loop from Eksel through Bosland.
quote: Cycling through the Trees – Butterfly Valley Lommel Loop - Distance: 16.2 km; Duration: 57 minutes; Difficulty: Easy; Starting Point: Natuurreservaat Veewei... De Boom In by Will Beckers – Cycling through the Trees Loop - Distance: 18.1 km

claim: Visit Limburg cancelled the planned fifth 'Fietsen onder de Grond' (Cycling Underground) installation in Riemst in September 2025 due to insufficient local support; the four realised experiences are Water (Bokrijk), Trees (Bosland), Heathland and Mine Terrils (both Hoge Kempen).
quote: Visit Limburg decided to stop the 'Cycling Underground' project in the Mergelland because, although the second permit application was positively assessed, there was insufficient local support... the other 4 cycling experiences that were successfully realized include 'Cycling through Water' in Bokrijk, 'Cycling through the Trees' in National Park Bosland, 'Cycling through the Heathland,' and 'Cycling among the Mine Terrils'

claim: Independent travel blog describes Cycling Through the Trees as 'a fabulous and thrilling gimmick' and 'utterly wonderful', confirming the experience lives up to the marketing for a destination ride.
quote: The blog review from 'Notes from Camelid Country' describes it as a fabulous and thrilling gimmick, and utterly wonderful, showing how the Flemish region of Limburg has gone the extra mile to lure cyclists to the region
